How to use the GoldAlert Commodity Dashboard

GoldAlert added oil, copper, natural gas and platinum to give precious-metals investors a wider macro view. Here is how to read it properly — and the one thing to check first before drawing any conclusions from the numbers.

Start with the timestamp, not the price

Open the Commodity Dashboard and look for the "Daily dataset updated" line before anything else. Each commodity card also shows its own observation date. This matters because different markets close at different times — the New York oil close happens hours after the London gold fix, and some markets observe public holidays that others do not. A current page can show closes from different sessions, so confirming which date each number represents prevents you from comparing apples to oranges.

What each card shows

Every commodity card has the same four-part structure:

  1. Name and unit — the benchmark being tracked and whether the price is per barrel, per pound or per troy ounce.
  2. Latest close — the most recent scheduled daily close in US dollars.
  3. Daily change — the percentage move from the previous observation.
  4. Short summary — a one-line description with a link to the dedicated commodity page for more context.

The four assets cover different parts of the macro picture. WTI crude oil reflects energy costs and global consumption expectations. Copper tracks industrial activity across construction, manufacturing and clean technology. Natural gas is a regional, weather-sensitive market that does not always move with the others. Platinum connects industrial demand (especially automotive and clean energy) with precious-metal investment demand.

Move from a price to a relationship

A daily price tells you what one market did. A ratio tells you what it did relative to another — which is often more informative. After reviewing the commodity cards, open Market Ratios to see Gold/Copper, Gold/Oil, Gold/Platinum and Bitcoin/Gold alongside each other.

One thing worth keeping in mind: the formula direction matters. Gold/Copper and Gold/Oil place gold in the numerator, so a rising ratio means gold is strengthening relative to the commodity. Bitcoin/Gold flips that: Bitcoin is in the numerator, so a rising ratio means Bitcoin is strengthening relative to gold. Always check the formula label on the ratio page before interpreting a direction.

A five-minute workflow that actually works

  1. Check the update timestamp and confirm the observation dates on each card.
  2. Identify the largest daily mover — what changed the most since yesterday?
  3. Click through to that commodity's dedicated page and read the context.
  4. Open the related ratio to separate absolute price from relative performance.
  5. Ask what evidence would change your interpretation before acting on it.

What this dashboard is not

These are daily scheduled closes — not live streaming prices, not executable quotes, and not trading recommendations. If you are actively trading any of these markets, you need a live data feed from a licensed source. GoldAlert is built for education and research, which means zooming out and building context rather than reacting to the last tick.

Frequently asked questions

Are these live tradable quotes?

No. They are scheduled daily closes intended for educational analysis. For live trading, use a licensed real-time data provider.

Why does the update timestamp matter?

It prevents you from comparing observations from different trading sessions, which can produce misleading percentage changes.
